episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 113: Chlorpyrifos/Paraoxon Phosphorylated Human AChE vs. Aged Dealkylated Adduct (PDB 5HF5 / 5HF6 / 5HFA), Pralidoxime Reactivation Window, RBC vs. Plasma Cholinesterase & Eddleston RCT. In the emergency department, suction clears the airway and the cardiac rate rises. Hours later, the person still cannot sustain ventilation. The Critical Care Clinician follows breathing, perfusion and strength. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows a phosphorus atom from a pesticide oxon to a covalent bond on acetylcholinesterase, then asks what makes that bond harder to undo. The patient, dialogue and individual measurements are fictional. Chapter 132, “Acetylcholinesterase and its Inhibitors,” in the live Pharmacology notebook’s *Primer on the Autonomic Nervous System* (2012), names parathion and discusses paraoxon, inhibition and aging. The clinical case concerns a different diethyl pesticide, chlorpyrifos. Pharmacology notebook
